chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who is greeted while he is in prayer. He said: 'He replies with 'Salamun 'Alaykum' (Peace be upon you) and does not say 'Wa 'Alaykum as-Salam' (And upon you be peace), for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was standing in prayer when 'Ammar ibn Yasir passed by him and 'Ammar greeted him. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) replied like this.'

key_terms.وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ: And upon you be peace (full greeting)

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim reply to a greeting while performing prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of responding to greetings during prayer, distinguishing between the obligatory greeting ('Salamun 'Alaykum') and the optional response ('Wa 'Alaykum as-Salam') to maintain ritual focus. It grounds this ruling in the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), who demonstrated this brevity when greeted by 'Ammar ibn Yasir, a key companion in Shia tradition. This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on adhering strictly to prophetic practice while avoiding unnecessary speech that might invalidate or distract from the prayer.
